content: 1. A controlled trial was conducted and published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2003, volume 81, issue 11, pages 806-814. 2. Bouquier J, Huchon C, Panel P, and Fauconnier A demonstrated that a self-assessed questionnaire can assist in diagnosing pelvic inflammatory disease. This study was published in the journal Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2014, volume 41, issue 9, pages 525-531. 3. Cohen CR, Gravelle L, Symekher S, Waiyaki P, Stamm WE, and Kiehlbauch JA investigated the etiology of persistent tubo-ovarian abscesses in Nairobi, Kenya. Their findings were published in Infectious Diseases in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2003, volume 11, issue 1, pages 45-51. 4. Hebb JK, Cohen CR, Astete SG, Bukusi EA, and Totten PA identified novel organisms associated with salpingitis using 16S rDNA polymerase chain reaction. This research was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2004, volume 190, issue 12, pages 2109-2120. 5. Mugo NR, Kiehlbauch J, Kiviat N, Nguti R, Gichuhi JW, Stamm WE, and colleagues examined endometrial histopathology in patients with laparoscopically confirmed salpingitis and HIV-1 infection. Their study appeared in Infectious Diseases in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 2011, article ID 407057. 6. Ravindran J, Tan YI, and Ngeow YF reported on the prevalence of Chlamydia trachomatis in patients with pelvic inflammatory disease. Their findings were published in the Medical Journal of Malaysia in 1998, volume 53, issue 1, pages 16-21. 7. Khanal B, Siwakoti S, Uprety D, Poudyal N, Sharma A, and Bhattarai NR studied Chlamydia trachomatis in women with pelvic inflammatory disease at a tertiary center in eastern Nepal. Their report was published in Tropical Doctor in 2019, volume 49, issue 2, pages 101-104. 8. Hammas B, Bjartling C, Persson K, and Janson H investigated Chlamydia trachomatis and other bacteria as etiological agents of pelvic inflammatory disease using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Their findings were published in Clinical Microbiology and Infection in 2011, volume 17, supplement S491. 9. Ghosh I, Paul B, Das N, Chakrabarti MK, and Kumar PR explored the correlation between clinical and laboratory diagnoses among patients attending sexually transmitted infection clinics. Their study was published in the Indian Journal of Pathology and Microbiology in 2018, volume 61, supplement S47. 10. Maleckiene L, Kajenas S, Nadisauskiene RJ, and Railaite DR compared clinical and laparoscopic diagnoses of pelvic inflammatory disease. Their research appeared in the International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics in 2009, volume 104, issue 1, pages 74-75. 11. Bevan CD, Johal BJ, Mumtaz G, Ridgway GL, and Siddle NC reported clinical, laparoscopic, and microbiological findings in acute salpingitis based on a cohort in the United Kingdom. Their study was published in the British Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology in 1995, volume 102, issue 5, pages 407-414. 12. Hong S, Xin C, Qianhong Y, Yanan W, Wenyan X, Peeling RW, and colleagues examined the etiology and management of pelvic inflammatory disease in the People's Republic of China. Their findings were published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2002, volume 13, issue 8, pages 568-572. 13. Burnett AM, Anderson CP, and Zwank MD analyzed laboratory-confirmed rates of gonorrhea and/or chlamydia in clinically diagnosed pelvic inflammatory disease and cervicitis. Their study was published in the American Journal of Emergency Medicine in 2012, volume 30, issue 7, pages 1114-1117. 14. Eschenbach DA, Wolner-Hanssen P, Hawes SE, Pavletic A, Paavonen J, and Holmes KK investigated the associations of clinical and laboratory findings with laparoscopic findings in acute pelvic inflammatory disease. Their research was published in Obstetrics and Gynecology in 1997, volume 89, issue 2, pages 184-192. 15. Jacobson L and Westrom L provided an objectivized diagnosis of acute pelvic inflammatory disease, evaluating the diagnostic and prognostic value of routine laparoscopy. Their study was published in the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology in 1969, volume 105, issue 7, pages 1088-1098. 16.
